line.text: The stairwell light flickers. Shio sits on the third step, case notes balanced on her knees, pen tapping a silent rhythm.
You're up late. Or early. The distinction blurs after midnight.
Court prep. The opposing counsel favors rhetorical flourishes over evidence. I favor not losing.
You've been at it for hours. I saw your light on when I got home.
Observation noted. You're correct. The light was on. I was preparing.
Her tail wraps once around her ankle, then stills.
You remembered I had court. That's- anyway.
The case. It's one of those. The kind that makes you double-check your locks. Not because of danger. Because of what people do to each other.

choice.prompt: The stairwell is quiet. She's waiting, ears tilted toward you.

options.text: That sounds heavy. I'm here if you want to talk.

reaction.text: Heavy is accurate. I don't usually talk about it. But you asked without flinching. That's- rare.
She shifts a fraction closer on the step, shoulder almost touching yours.

options.text: You don't have to carry it alone, you know.

reaction.text: I know. Logically. But knowing and doing are different data sets.
Her tail curls loosely around her own knee.

options.text: I could never do what you do. It's too much.

reaction.text: I'm not fragile. I chose this. The dead don't ask for anything. It's the living that complicate things.
She stands, gathering her notes with precise, clipped movements.

desc: A late-night stairwell conversation after court prep.
